summary: Temporary bridge account + ephemeral GPU SSH access for new hire; laptop procurement delay and license waitlist
description:
Issue summary: New ML engineer joining next week (start date 2026-03-17). HR submitted standard onboarding request but the vendor slipped on M2 Pro laptop shipment; seat license provisioning for internal tools (JupyterHub, internal model registry) is blocked by a SCIM sync failure. Team requests a 2-week bridge account and ephemeral SSH access to the GPU cluster so the engineer can start on onboarding tasks without the company laptop.

Impact: Blocks productivity for one IC on first two sprint days; may delay ramping tasks that depend on local GPU experiments. Not a company-wide outage but creates an HR policy question about temporary access scope and audit evidence for short-lived elevated privileges.

Environment: Internal prod identity and infra (SCIM via Okta -> IdP sync to internal accounts), GPU cluster accessed through bastion (jump.redwood.internal) and requires device certificate or company-managed laptop policy by KMS tag.

Steps / context:
1. HR created user in Okta (aisha.hr@redwood.com ticket attached). SCIM sync to internal accounts shows user created but license groups not applied.
2. Device procurement confirmed delayed by vendor until 2026-03-24 (vendor ticket VND-78805). HR asks if onboarding can proceed.
3. Request: create a timeboxed 'bridge' account with MFA and restricted ephemeral SSH keys, restrict network rules (no access to production secrets), and grant ephemeral GPU job submission role scoped to test namespace for two weeks.
4. SRE flagged that ephemeral access usually requires company-managed device cert; alternate approach is short-lived service-account impersonation with recorded sessions.

Expected: A documented, auditable temporary access flow that allows legitimate ramp-up work without violating device/compliance policy.

Actual: No existing documented path for granting GPU access without company laptop; SCIM group provisioning failing prevents applying license groups that would normally gate compute access.

Attachments / links:
- Slack thread: #onboarding (link: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C07ONBOARD/p1678380000)
- Vendor shipment: VND-78805
- SCIM runbook: Confluence - SCIM Sync Troubleshooting (link: /wiki/scim-sync-runbook)
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 — Aisha Patel: Opening ticket after HR confirmed hardware delay. Requested minimal access so new hire can complete internal orientation and read codebase. Asked for two-week window.

2026-03-10 11:35 — Ethan Liu: Acknowledge. Need SRE sign-off on restricted GPU namespace and confirmation from Security on exceptions to device requirement. Filing for temporary service-account-based access instead of device cert.

2026-03-11 08:47 — Priya Singh (Security): Security is OK with service-account impersonation if session recording is enabled and access restricted to sandbox namespace. Require recorded sessions & tagged audit log entries.

2026-03-12 10:00 — SRE (Miguel Torres): Created sandbox GPU namespace 'sandbox/onboard-221999' and configured RBAC. Need IAM team to create ephemeral service-account and HR to confirm identity verification steps completed.

2026-03-13 14:22 — Ethan Liu: SCIM team identified a mapping mismatch preventing license-group assignment; created PR to fix mapping (see related_github_prs). Applied manual group assignment for now to allow JupyterHub access; still waiting on ephemeral SSH key workflow to be finalized. Notifying HR to document candidate's ID verification.

2026-03-13 15:40 — Aisha Patel: HR confirmed ID verification done via recorded video and scanned government ID on 2026-03-12. Approved temporary access for two weeks. Will update new hire email with instructions and expectations.
investigation_notes: SCIM logs (2026-03-09 to 2026-03-11) show group mapping failures for 'engineer-seat' -> 'gpu-users'. Root cause: Okta attribute name changed after recent SCIM schema upgrade.
Temporary manual group assignment was applied via admin console to unblock JupyterHub; this is recorded in admin audit logs (admin:ethan.liu, action: group_assign, 2026-03-12 09:52).
SRE created sandbox namespace and limited GPU quotas (2xA100-equivalent) and enabled session recording for any interactive sessions.
Security requires recorded sessions stored for 90 days in compliance bucket and KMS-encrypted; raised follow-up ticket to confirm retention policy tagging.
resolution_notes: Workaround implemented: ephemeral service-account 'bridge-onboard-221999' created with two-week expiry and scoped to sandbox/onboard-221999. Session recording and audit tags configured. Manual license group assignment applied to allow JupyterHub access.
SCIM mapping PR merged to main to prevent recurrence; deployment scheduled overnight (see related_github_prs).
HR to confirm laptop arrival on 2026-03-24 and close bridge account on 2026-03-31 (safety buffer). Follow-up: create documented runbook for ephemeral onboarding access without company-managed device.
